title: Donald Trump sparks health concerns as Fox News host forced to remind him of quote he once said - NewsBreak
text:
By Connor McCrory ,
31 minutes ago President Donald Trump appeared briefly caught off guard Wednesday when a Fox News correspondent reminded him of a statement he made about Iran in 2020.
The exchange came during a news conference in France, where Trump was asked by Fox News correspondent Peter Doocy about his past description of Iran as a country that "never won a war but never lost a negotiation."
"I just want to ask you about this," Doocy said. "A wise man once said in January of 2020, Iran never won a war but never lost a negotiation." Trump responded, "Who said that?". The bizarre moment came ahead of Trump shouting 'it's signed' as he inked an Iran deal at a Versailles dinner .

Doocy responded, "Donald Trump," to which the president replied, "That’s what I thought you would say."
Doocy then asked how Trump planned to persuade Americans skeptical of the agreement that it should be viewed as a victory.
"So, so how do you go back to the United States and convince a skeptical American public that this deal is a win here they lost militarily," Doocy asked.
Trump answered by arguing that critics would attack him regardless of the outcome.
"OK, it’s very tough because," Trump said. "I know that no matter what, if I would go, by the way, if I’d go another three or four weeks, those same people that are critical would say he went too long, he should have done, you know, no matter what if they raise the white flag of surrender. And if they said praise be to Allah, Donald Trump is the greatest president ever. We totally concede, we totally give up. This war is over, we have failed. The New York Times and CNN and a couple of others, they’re not all that dishonest, they say. Iran had a great victory, OK."
Some social media users mocked Trump for not immediately recognizing the quote as his own, while others focused on his lengthy answer.
"What a f--king disgrace. He has no idea what he’s doing. He sounds like he’s on his last legs," one X user penned.
Another added, "Doocy about to be called a dumb son of a b--ch by a second President."
"The internet never forgets. Especially when your own words become the counterargument," a third penned.
The exchange came amid Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif writing on X that leaders from the United States and Iran had signed a memorandum of agreement and that Pakistan and Qatar would host a formal ceremony Friday in Switzerland. Sharif briefly removed the post before reposting similar language without the reference to Friday’s ceremony, creating uncertainty over whether the event would proceed.
Trump said he had signed the document at the Palace of Versailles.
"It’s signed," Trump said as he left Versailles. "I signed it in Versailles. Just signed it."
